text:
Lina Brooks: Heads-up — we started seeing malformed cache TTLs from the edge header parser in apac regions at ~03:40 UTC. Result: embeddings tail latency spiked and realtime streams saw intermittent truncated frames. Investigating.

Devon Park: How widespread? customer-facing errors or just internal retries?

Lina Brooks: Impacted traffic routed through legacy edge POPs. ~7 customers saw 5xx/connection resets, ~200 customers saw increased latency for embeddings and streaming. No data loss.

ops-bot: incident-severity: SEV3 (customer-impacting latency/errors).

Arman Singh: Mitigations in flight: 1) toggled off ff-edge-cache-ttl-opt 2) issued targeted cache purge for apac POPs 3) temporarily pinned routing to modern POPs for streaming endpoints.

Devon Park: Any quick commands for SRE to verify purge?

Arman Singh: Use rdwctl cache inspect + purge:

```bash
# inspect problematic TTLs
rdwctl cache inspect --region apac --filter "edge_header_ttl"
# purge caches for embedding/streaming routes
rdwctl cache purge --region apac --routes "embed,streaming" --concurrency 8
```

CS-bot: Draft customer bulletin posted to #support-digest: https://status.redwood-inference.com/incidents/2895018000 — contains impact window and mitigation steps.

Lina Brooks: Metrics: embedding p95 returned to baseline by 03:58 UTC after purge + rollback. Streaming reconnect rates dropped to normal by 04:05 UTC. We're keeping throttles for a short window to avoid fanout.

Devon Park: Assign follow-ups: Arman to write the timeline + root cause, Lina to add a CI guard against header parser opt toggles without canary, CS to publish customer note + opt-in followup. Target RCA + bulletin by EOD.

Arman Singh: I'll open the RCA draft and PR for the CI guard today.

Lina Brooks: Thanks everyone. Leaving this thread pinned for the RCA in case we need more context. :pin:
